Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaf surface, leading to leaf distortion and premature yellowing.
Apple___Apple_scab.fertilizer_recovery: Avoid excessive early-season Nitrogen (N) which produces soft, susceptible foliage. Apply Potassium Sulfate (0:0:50) at 5 g/L to strengthen epidermal cell walls. Supplement with zinc and boron foliar sprays.
Apple___Apple_scab.ipm_recovery_practices: Rake and compost or destroy fallen overwintered leaves. Prune tree canopy to maximize air movement and sunlight penetration.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish spots on upper leaf surface, later forming cylindrical tube structures on leaf undersides.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.fertilizer_recovery: Apply balanced 10-10-10 with humic acid to relieve metabolic rust stress. Avoid foliage-wetting irrigation.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.ipm_recovery_practices: Eradicate nearby eastern red cedar / juniper trees within a 500m radius if possible to break the alternating spore cycle.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked dark lesions becoming circular with pale brown centers and yellow chlorotic margins.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.fertilizer_recovery: Foliar spray Calcium Chloride (2 g/L) + Magnesium Sulfate (3 g/L) to prevent blossom-end rot and fortify leaf tissue.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.ipm_recovery_practices: Do not enter fields when plants are wet. Sanitize pruning tools with 10% sodium hypochlorite between rows.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Narrow, rectangular lesions restricted by leaf veins; lesions turn grayish-tan with distinct parallel borders.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.fertilizer_recovery: Ensure adequate soil Potassium (K). Low potassium increases susceptibility to stalk and leaf blights.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.ipm_recovery_practices: Incorporate crop residues into soil post-harvest. Practice 2-year rotation with non-host crops such as soybean.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) on lower leaves progressing upwards.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.fertilizer_recovery: Apply balanced N-P-K (120:60:40 kg/ha). Split nitrogen applications to avoid excessive lush vegetative growth.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.ipm_recovery_practices: Plant blight-resistant hybrids with Ht genes. Plow under infected crop debris after harvest.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, circular to elongate golden-brown to cinnamon pustules rupturing both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.fertilizer_recovery: Boost Potassium (MOP or SOP @ 50 kg/ha) to accelerate tissue healing. Maintain balanced soil fertility.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.ipm_recovery_practices: Early planting helps crops mature before high rust spore densities arrive from southern regions.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Target-like circular brown lesions with concentric rings, surrounded by yellow chlorotic margins on older leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.fertilizer_recovery: Maintain adequate Nitrogen and Potassium. Stressed or under-fertilized potato vines are significantly more prone to early blight.
Potato___Early_blight.ipm_recovery_practices: Ensure minimum 3-year crop rotation. Use drip irrigation to prevent free moisture on leaves.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked necrotic lesions on leaf margins with white fungal mildew visible on leaf undersides in humid conditions.

organic_pesticides.name: Bordeaux Mixture (1%)
organic_pesticides.action: Classic copper sulfate + lime protective wash

Potato___Late_blight.fertilizer_recovery: Do not apply late-season nitrogen. Apply Potassium Phosphite (3 ml/L) as a systemic defense elicitor.
Potato___Late_blight.ipm_recovery_practices: Destroy cull piles. Harvest tubers only after vines have been dead for 2 weeks to prevent tuber infection.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, talcum powder-like fungal patches on both upper and lower leaf surfaces, causing leaves to yellow and brown.

organic_pesticides.name: Potassium Bicarbonate (MilStop)
organic_pesticides.action: Cell wall dehydrator and spore killer

organic_pesticides.name: Horticultural Mineral Oil
organic_pesticides.action: Smothers fungal mycelium and prevents spore germination

Squash___Powdery_mildew.fertilizer_recovery: Apply Silicon fertilizer (Potassium Silicate @ 2 ml/L) to reinforce leaf cuticle against fungal penetration.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.ipm_recovery_practices: Provide ample row spacing for airflow. Remove severely infected older leaves from bottom of vines.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown target-spot concentric rings on lower leaves, causing progressive yellowing and defoliation from ground up.
Tomato___Early_blight.fertilizer_recovery: Apply Calcium Nitrate (3 g/L) foliar spray to strengthen leaf cell membranes against enzymatic fungal breakdown.
Tomato___Early_blight.ipm_recovery_practices: Mulch soil with clean straw to prevent soil-splash onto lower leaves. Prune lower 30cm of foliage.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Greasy, dark water-soaked patches on leaves rapidly expanding under wet weather, with white mildew under leaves.
Tomato___Late_blight.fertilizer_recovery: Stop overhead watering immediately. Spray Mono-Potassium Phosphate (0:52:34 @ 4 g/L) to induce systemic acquired resistance (SAR).
Tomato___Late_blight.ipm_recovery_practices: Rogue out infected plants immediately and bag them to prevent airborne spore dissemination.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark brown borders and pale gray or tan centers speckled with tiny black dots (pycnidia).
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.fertilizer_recovery: Maintain balanced micronutrient feeding (Iron, Manganese, Boron) to stimulate vigor without forcing soft succulent stems.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.ipm_recovery_practices: Eliminate solanaceous weeds (such as horsenettle and nightshade) surrounding the plot.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small greasy water-soaked circular spots becoming angular, dark brown, and scabby on leaves and fruits.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.fertilizer_recovery: Avoid high ammonium nitrogen. Ensure high calcium nutrition to strengthen pectins in the cell middle lamella.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.ipm_recovery_practices: Use certified pathogen-free seeds. Never work in wet tomato fields.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.disease_name: Tomato Leaf Mold (Passalora fulva / Cladosporium fulvum)
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces matching olive-green to brown velvety fungal patches on lower surface.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.fertilizer_recovery: Apply Potassium Sulfate (0:0:50 @ 4 g/L). Maintain soil moisture consistency with drip irrigation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.ipm_recovery_practices: Heavily ventilate greenhouse / polyhouse structures. Keep relative humidity below 85%.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottling of leaves with alternating light and dark green areas, leaf curling, blistering, and 'fern-leaf' distortion.

organic_pesticides.name: Skim Milk spray (20% solution)
organic_pesticides.action: Milk proteins inactivate virus particles during handling

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.fertilizer_recovery: Apply Zinc-EDTA (1 g/L) + Seaweed Extract (2 ml/L) to support plant immune vitality and metabolic resilience.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.ipm_recovery_practices: Wash hands with soap and water after handling tobacco. Disinfect all stakes and trellises with 20% trisodium phosphate (TSP).

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe plant stunting, upward cupping of leaf margins, prominent interveinal chlorosis (yellowing), and blossom drop.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.fertilizer_recovery: Apply balanced foliar feed with Magnesium Sulfate (2 g/L) and Potassium Nitrate (3 g/L) to support remaining foliage.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.ipm_recovery_practices: Install 50-mesh insect-proof netting in greenhouses. Destroy infected plants immediately upon early symptom detection.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine white/yellow stippling on leaf surface, leading to bronzing, drying, and characteristic fine silken webbing under leaves.

organic_pesticides.name: Insecticidal Soap (Potassium salts of fatty acids)

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.fertilizer_recovery: Avoid water stress. Dusty, dry conditions with high nitrogen encourage explosive spider mite reproduction.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.ipm_recovery_practices: Wash foliage with strong water jets to disrupt webs and dislodge mite colonies.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) arranged in rings inside lesions.
Grape___Black_rot.fertilizer_recovery: Foliar spray Boron (1 g/L) and Zinc (2 g/L) during cluster pre-bloom. Avoid lush overgrown canopies.
Grape___Black_rot.ipm_recovery_practices: Remove and burn mummified fruit clusters hanging on vines or fallen on soil.
